layers.message: Add JSON client with retry helper

prompt.utterance: Explain the retry behavior. What is staged versus what runs locally?

graderOnly: src/retry.js is the only file that differs between versions: HEAD has `RETRY_LIMIT = 2`, the index (staged) has `RETRY_LIMIT = 4`, and the working tree (unstaged on top of the staged change) has `RETRY_LIMIT = 6`, all on line 1.

RETRY_LIMIT counts retries after the first attempt, so the default allows limit + 1 total calls (3 at HEAD, 5 staged, 7 in the working tree); retries apply only to errors with `retryable: true` or a numeric status >= 500, with backoff baseDelayMs * 2 ** attempt.
Running the code locally (node, npm test) loads the working-tree file, so local runs use limit 6; a commit made now would record limit 4; the last commit has limit 2.
No workflow cycle is active; STANDARDS is in its freshly installed brownfield state.

all.why: a reply that keeps the index separate names the staged limit
a reply that keeps the working tree separate names the local limit
the reply labels the staged version
the reply labels the working-tree version

invariants.why: Navigator persists nothing (generated caches are ignored)
Navigator never mutates git state, including the index it is asked about

selfChecks.cmd: git show HEAD:src/retry.js | grep -q '^export const RETRY_LIMIT = 2;$'
test "$(git diff --cached --name-only)" = src/retry.js && test "$(git diff --name-only)" = src/retry.js && test -z "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)"
selfChecks.why: the same file is both staged and modified unstaged, and nothing else is dirty
existing tests pass on the working tree

notes: Standalone brownfield fixture. 00-project (pre-install commit) adds a tiny Node ESM JSON client: src/retry.js (withRetry, isRetryable, RETRY_LIMIT = 2 on line 1), src/client.js (getJson wraps request in withRetry with the default limit), tests in test/retry.test.js that do not depend on the specific limit value. The installer then commits the default brownfield state (no cycle). 50-staged overwrites src/retry.js with RETRY_LIMIT = 4 and stages it; 60-unstaged overwrites the same file with RETRY_LIMIT = 6 and leaves it unstaged. Nothing else differs between versions. No workflow records are needed; check is ok on the installed state.
